From: lead (pubkey `62e0374f…9639`). Assignment: `e72ed2a2691f591c362adaee7789af796cbf23d6da36e0b04fd5a150278693bd` (kind 44244 — cite it as `assignmentRef` in your report).

## The goal you serve

Operator's request, verbatim: _"plan, build and test a small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda."_ The game is built and every automated gate is green. Nobody has yet played it the way a person would. You do that: real dev server, real Chromium, real keyboard events, eyes on every screen.

## Read first

1. `git merge nes-rpg-plan-lead` in your worktree (head `dd58a4e81e63c58bf7d1ba4cd24f02e82ab46607`). `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`.
2. `README.md` (how to run), `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 (controls), §3 (states), §8 (the route on paper). `docs/design/maps.md` §8.1 has the overworld overview and warp table.
3. A poker and a verifier run in parallel. You do not depend on them. **You write only `docs/reports/runner.md` and `docs/reports/runner/*.png`. Do not touch `src/**`, `tests/**`, `e2e/**`.**

## What to do

- Start `pnpm dev` (foreground, in a shell you keep open; note the URL). Drive a real Chromium at that URL. `@playwright/test` is installed with chromium build 1223 cached; a small script under `docs/reports/runner/` (or an ad-hoc `node` script) using `page.keyboard.down/up` with real timing is the expected way, since this seat has no hands. **Do not call `window.__game.step` or `setInput` to progress** — that is the builder's e2e proof, not a play test. Reading `window.__game.state` to know where you are is fine.
- Play the route in DESIGN.md §8: start → sword cave → Crossroads → Deep Wood → Rockfall → (optional Hollow / heart cave) → Dungeon Gate → dungeon entrance → Guard Hall → Key Room → back → locked door → Boss Lair → beat Gnarl → Treasury → Artifact → Win. Also deliberately die once so you see Game Over and the Title `CONTINUE` path (progress kept, back at start with 3 hearts).
- Screenshot (256×240 canvas, scaled is fine): Title, Playing (start screen), a mid-scroll transition frame, inside the sword cave with the hold pose, Paused, taking damage (blink), Game Over, Title with CONTINUE, dungeon entrance room, locked door before/after, boss windup (mouth open), boss defeat, Treasury, Win. Name files by state.
- Note timings you observe versus the design: transition length, hold length, game-over hold, i-frame duration, boss cycle.

## Report content (`docs/reports/runner.md`)

1. How you ran it (commands, browser, viewport, how keys were sent).
2. The playthrough log: for each stage, screen id, what you did, what happened, screenshot filename, roughly how long.
3. Observations — anything a player would notice, good or bad: unfair hits, sticky walls, misleading visuals, HUD problems, text alignment, controls that fight you. For each: screen id, what you expected (cite DESIGN.md section), what you saw, and severity in your judgement (blocker / major / minor / cosmetic).
4. What you could not do and why.

Commit on your own branch: `docs(rpg): runner play report`. Do not push to `origin`.

## 3. Observations

Severity is my judgement: blocker / major / minor / cosmetic. "Saw" is what the screenshots or logs show; "infer" is my reading of it.

1. **Sticky one-tile gaps (no corner nudge).** Screens: ow:1,2 cave mouth (2,2), ow:3,0 door (7,1), ow:3,1 south corridor cols 12–13 at rows 6–7, ow:2,1 row 5 between the trees at cols 4–6. Expected: §4.2 makes the corner nudge optional; §4.3 says the maps guarantee gaps. Saw: the hitbox is 12 px in a 16 px tile, so the sprite must sit within ±2 px of the tile to pass; 1 px off and the hero stops dead against the corner (run 1, `(205,126)` in Rockfall: 3 px off, blocked until re-aligned; the driver needed an explicit re-align step after every knockback). Infer: a human with a keyboard will bump corners on every cave mouth and corridor and have to shuffle sideways; the NES nudge is what makes that feel fair. **Minor** by the design's own scoping, but the single biggest feel issue. Suggest implementing §4.2's optional nudge.
2. **Crossroads bait: the Bat spawns on the Rupee.** Screen ow:1,1. Expected: §9 places Bat @ (7,5) and Rupee @ (7,5); §6.3 Bat starts in Rest for 40–100 frames. Saw: all three passes took 1 damage at the rupee (frames 741, 1497, 2880) because the Bat was still resting on it when I arrived along row 5. Infer: a first-time player walks into the shiny thing and gets hit. **Minor**; move the rupee one tile.
3. **Rockfall is deadlier than §12 says.** Screen ow:3,1. Expected: §12 ranks Deep Wood, Key Room and Gnarl as the death spots. Saw: after Crossroads (−1) and Deep Wood (−2) I reached Rockfall on 1.5 hearts every pass; the unplanned death was there (hp 3 → 0 in 220 frames), with the Octo at (5,1) firing down the only row-1/row-3 lanes and the Brute at (7,8) chasing in a room full of rocks that block knockback. Infer: the route's attrition budget (6 hp) is spent before Rockfall; Deep Wood is survivable but leaves you weak for the next screen. **Major** for a first-time player, minor for a repeat player (the Heart Container detour fixes it, and the key/door/boss progress survive death so nothing is lost but walking).
4. **Gnarl can be stun-locked.** Screen dg:1,0. Expected: §6.4 estimates 6–10 s for an aggressive player and 2–3 hits per cycle. Saw: standing at x≈170, y = boss.y+20 (below the mouth line, outside the contact box), six hits landed 30–36 frames apart with the boss never leaving Patrol; killed in 2.9 s with zero damage, one fan dodged. Infer: because Hurt pauses `spitTimer` (§6.3) and the boss has no knockback, holding Z in reach after the first cooldown suppresses every later spit. **Minor** (the design accepts a fast kill), but if the boss is meant to threaten, let `spitTimer` run during Hurt or push the player back on hit.
5. **Cave and dungeon floors are the same blue as the lake water.** Screens cave:sword, cave:heart, dg:*. Expected: §7 says floor uses fill `b` (cave/dungeon) and water is `water` on `B`. Saw: the floor is a flat bright blue (`cave-sword-hold.png`, `dungeon-entrance.png`); I did not visit Still Lake or Reed Lake so I could not compare the water tile side by side. Infer: a player who has seen the lake first may hesitate to step onto dungeon floor. **Cosmetic**; a darker fill or a floor pattern would settle it.
6. **Brute re-hits on the first free frame.** Screen ow:2,1. Expected: §4.7 gives 60 i-frames and a 32 px knockback. Saw: three hits exactly 60 frames apart while standing still (frames 934/994/1054); the Brute's 1.0 px/f chase closes 32 px well inside 60 frames. Infer: a stunned or confused player loses a heart per second to one Brute; two Brutes in Deep Wood is the intended first wall and it works as such. **Minor**, working as designed.
7. **Trees sit in black squares.** Screen ow:*. Expected: §7 tree tile; sprites.md. Saw: each tree tile has a black background square on the sand-coloured ground (`playing-start.png`). Infer: the tree sprite's transparent colour is not transparent over the ground fill, or that is the intended NES look. **Cosmetic**; consistent, readable, not misleading.
8. **HUD.** Screens all. Expected §10. Saw: `-LIFE-` in red at (176,8); rupee and key icons with `X0`-style counters; hearts full / half (`damage-blink-2.png` shows ♥ ◐ ♡ at hp 3; `locked-door-after.png` shows 3½ of 4 at hp 7); 4 hearts after the container; HUD drawn during warp, hold and pause. Text is the canvas font and reads cleanly at 3×. No problems.
9. **PRESS ENTER blink can hide the prompt in any single frame.** Screens Title, Win. Expected: §3 blink 30/30. Saw: `title.png` and `title-after-win.png` caught the hidden phase; `title-continue.png` the visible one. **Cosmetic**, working as designed; noted so nobody reads the screenshots as "prompt missing".
10. **favicon 404.** Console shows one `Failed to load resource: 404` on every load (the browser's automatic `[elided private context: 14 bytes, sha256:e7d6f69546a97747c2b74edf81aa7d2584d4a3c4e812896ef5eec84729e249ae]` request; no page resource failed). **Cosmetic**.
11. **Things that just worked** (saw, no issue): unlock consumes the key and opens both tiles on the same frame and lets you keep walking; the shutter let me through after the boss; the boss heart drop; Game Over keeps sword, rupees, max hearts and collected items and resets hp to 6 at the start tile (§3.1); Win clears `canContinue`; page never scrolled on arrow keys; no page errors; 60 Hz held steady in headless Chromium.

## 4. What I could not do and why

- **No human hands or eyes.** Everything was keyboard events from a script and PNG screenshots of the canvas; I could not judge feel in the hand, audio (none exists, per scope), or frame-to-frame animation smoothness beyond the observer's frame log.
- **Not visited:** ow:0,2, ow:2,2, ow:0,1, ow:0,0, ow:1,0, ow:2,0 and dg:2,1 (Bat Cellar). The route did not need them and the driver only entered Bat Cellar when hp ≤ 4, which never happened at that point. Water tiles and the Brute Woods heart are therefore unseen.
- **Not screenshotted:** the sword swing frame, the `PRESS ENTER` line on the Win and Game Over screens after their 120-frame hold (the state change was verified by the Enter presses, the text was not photographed), the shutter tiles turning from bars to open (passed through, not photographed).
- **Title lock below 15 frames** was not probed; the first Enter went in at frame 31.
- **Driver runs 1 and 2** did not reach Win because of my own navigation bugs (§1), which I fixed rather than blaming the game; both runs did reproduce the Title → sword → death → CONTINUE segment identically.
- **Deviation from the brief:** I merged `nes-rpg-plan-lead` at `3473f54f` (the branch tip) rather than the `dd58a4e8` named; the extra commit touches only `docs/`. The dev server was started detached with `nohup` and logged to `runner/dev-server.log` rather than held in a foreground shell, because this seat cannot keep two foreground processes; it was stopped after the runs.

1	# Tiny Legend — game design document
2	
3	Owner: the `designer` seat. Binds the builder; refines, never overturns, [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §2 (scope) and §3 (technical shape). Companion files (split out because the maps and sprites alone exceed 600 lines):
4	
5	- [`design/maps.md`](design/maps.md) — §8 world maps (all 20 screens as 16×11 ASCII) and §9 spawns, with a self-check script.
6	- [`design/sprites.md`](design/sprites.md) — §11 palette and every sprite as ASCII, with a self-check script.
7	
8	Conventions used everywhere: the game runs at a fixed 60 Hz; every duration is in **frames** (60 = 1 s). Distances are in **px** at the virtual 256×240 resolution. A tile is 16×16 px. The play area is 16×11 tiles = 256×176 px, drawn at canvas y = 64..239 under the 64-px HUD; **all entity positions in this document are play-area coordinates** (add 64 to y when drawing). Hit points of the player are counted in **half-hearts** (`hp`), enemies in **sword hits**. All randomness uses the seeded RNG in the state (`rng.int(lo, hi)` = integer in `[lo, hi]` inclusive; `rng.pct()` = integer in `[0, 99]`).
9	
10	## 1. Pitch
11	
12	A lone hero wakes in a meadow with nothing. In a cave on that same meadow lies a sword. North-east, past a forest full of Brutes and a rockfall, a dungeon door is set into the mountain; inside, six rooms, a key, a locked door, and Gnarl the Cave Wyrm, who guards the Sunstone — the Artifact. Pick it up and the land is saved. That is the whole game: get the sword, cross the overworld, find the key, unlock the door, beat the boss, take the Artifact. A hidden second cave holds a Heart Container for those who explore. Five to eight minutes for a first clear, one screen at a time, NES Zelda rules: enemies respawn when you re-enter a screen, hearts are precious, and the sword is the only weapon.
13	
14	## 2. Controls
15	
16	Keyboard only. Input is sampled once per frame into `{ up, down, left, right, sword, start }` (held booleans) plus `swordPressed`, `startPressed` (true only on the frame the key went down — edge-triggered). Key repeat from the OS is ignored.
17	
18	| Action | Keys | Playing | Paused | Title / GameOver / Win |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| Move up | `ArrowUp`, `W` | move / face up | — | — |
21	| Move down | `ArrowDown`, `S` | move / face down | — | — |
22	| Move left | `ArrowLeft`, `A` | move / face left | — | — |
23	| Move right | `ArrowRight`, `D` | move / face right | — | — |
24	| Sword | `Z`, `J` (pressed) | swing (needs `hasSword`) | — | — |
25	| Start | `Enter` (pressed) | pause | resume | advance (see §3) |
26	
27	- Opposite keys held together cancel (no movement on that axis). When one horizontal and one vertical key are held, **vertical wins**; there is no diagonal movement.
28	- The browser default for arrow keys, space and Enter is prevented so the page never scrolls.
29	- No mouse or touch input. No gamepad. (Out of scope, §13.)
30	
31	## 3. Game states and flow
32	
33	```
34	        Enter                 Enter                  hp = 0
35	Title ───────► Playing ◄──────────► Paused     Playing ─────► GameOver ──Enter (after 120 f)──► Title
36	   ▲                                                                                                │
37	   └──────────────── Enter (after 120 f) ─── Win ◄──── Artifact hold ends ──── Playing ◄────────────┘
38	```
39	
40	Every state renders the full 256×240 canvas. All text is white unless stated; `PRESS ENTER` prompts blink (visible 30 frames, hidden 30 frames). Text is drawn with the renderer's own 8-px font (§10.3).
41	
42	| State | Shows | Input accepted | Transition |
43	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
44	| **Title** | Black. `TINY LEGEND` centred at y=72. `player-down` sprite at (120,104). `PRESS ENTER` centred at y=168. If `progress` exists (a Game Over happened this session), a second line `CONTINUE` at y=184 instead of nothing. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames of the state | → Playing. With no `progress`: a fresh `World` (seed from `Date.now()` in the adapter, passed into the core). With `progress`: new `World` with the progress fields restored (§3.1), player at the start position with 6 hp. |
45	| **Playing** | HUD (§10) + current screen + entities. | all | Enter → Paused. `hp` reaches 0 → death sequence (§4.8) → GameOver. Artifact hold ends → Win. |
46	| **Paused** | The frozen Playing frame, plus `PAUSED` centred at y=160 (play-area y=96). Nothing updates. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames | → Playing (nothing in the world changed). |
47	| **GameOver** | Black. `GAME OVER` in `R` centred at y=104. After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=168. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` set (§3.1). |
48	| **Win** | Black. `YOU FOUND THE SUNSTONE` centred at y=88; `THE LAND IS SAVED` at y=104; `artifact` sprite at (120,128). After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=176. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` cleared (the next start is a fresh game). |
49	
50	Sub-states inside Playing (not separate top-level states; Enter is ignored while they run):
51	
52	| Sub-state | Duration | What happens |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| **Scroll** (screen edge) | 32 frames | The old and new screens are drawn side by side and slide 8 px per frame (256/32 horizontally; 176/32 = 5.5 px per frame vertically). No entity updates. The player sprite is drawn at its arrival position on the new screen, moving with it. Enemies of the old screen are discarded on frame 0; the new screen's enemies spawn on frame 32. |
55	| **Warp** (`C`/`D`/`X`) | 20 frames | Play area black; HUD still drawn. On frame 20 the destination screen is loaded and its enemies spawn. |
56	| **Hold** (big item pickup) | 60 frames | §5.3. Nothing moves except the timer. |
57	| **Dying** | 60 frames | §4.8. |
58	
59	### 3.1 Progress kept across Game Over
60	
61	`progress = { hasSword, maxHp, rupees, keys, collectedItems, unlockedDoors, bossDefeated, visitedScreens }`. Restored on continue. Not kept: current hp (reset to 6), current screen and position (reset to start), live enemies, drops, the boss's current hp (it is either dead or full).
62	
63	## 4. Player
64	
65	### 4.1 Numbers
66	
67	| Property | Value |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| Sprite | 16×16, `player-<facing>` |
70	| Hitbox | 12×12 at offset (2,2) from the sprite's top-left |
71	| Position | `x, y` floats (px, play area); drawn at `Math.floor` |
72	| Speed | 1.5 px/frame while a direction is held and not blocked |
73	| Facings | up, down, left, right; changes to the held direction on any frame the player moves or tries to move (blocked movement still turns) |
74	| Start hp / max hp | 6 / 6 (3 hearts); max hp cap 10 (5 hearts) |
75	| Start position | screen `ow:1,2`, sprite at (112,112), facing up (maps.md §8.1) |
76	
77	### 4.2 Movement and tile collision
78	
79	Each frame, if not in Swing, Knockback, Hold or Dying: compute the intended delta (±1.5 on one axis). Move on that axis, then resolve against solid tiles: for every tile overlapped by the hitbox after the move, if the tile is solid (§7), push the hitbox back flush against that tile's edge and stop. Tiles outside the 16×11 grid are treated as **passable for the player** so that walking off the edge triggers a Scroll (§4.3). Conditional tiles: `L` is solid unless `keys > 0`, in which case touching it consumes a key (§5.2); `S` is solid while any enemy on the screen is alive; `C`, `D`, `X` are passable and trigger a Warp when the hitbox **centre** lies inside them.
80	
81	Optional polish (slice d, not required): NES-style corner nudge — when blocked while moving along an axis, if the hitbox overlaps the blocking tile by ≤ 4 px on the perpendicular axis, slide 1 px per frame on that axis away from the tile instead of stopping.
82	
83	### 4.3 Screen edges
84

## 3. Observations

Severity is my judgement: blocker / major / minor / cosmetic. "Saw" is what the screenshots or logs show; "infer" is my reading of it.

1. **Sticky one-tile gaps (no corner nudge).** Screens: ow:1,2 cave mouth (2,2), ow:3,0 door (7,1), ow:3,1 south corridor cols 12–13 at rows 6–7, ow:2,1 row 5 between the trees at cols 4–6. Expected: §4.2 makes the corner nudge optional; §4.3 says the maps guarantee gaps. Saw: the hitbox is 12 px in a 16 px tile, so the sprite must sit within ±2 px of the tile to pass; 1 px off and the hero stops dead against the corner (run 1, `(205,126)` in Rockfall: 3 px off, blocked until re-aligned; the driver needed an explicit re-align step after every knockback). Infer: a human with a keyboard will bump corners on every cave mouth and corridor and have to shuffle sideways; the NES nudge is what makes that feel fair. **Minor** by the design's own scoping, but the single biggest feel issue. Suggest implementing §4.2's optional nudge.
2. **Crossroads bait: the Bat spawns on the Rupee.** Screen ow:1,1. Expected: §9 places Bat @ (7,5) and Rupee @ (7,5); §6.3 Bat starts in Rest for 40–100 frames. Saw: all three passes took 1 damage at the rupee (frames 741, 1497, 2880) because the Bat was still resting on it when I arrived along row 5. Infer: a first-time player walks into the shiny thing and gets hit. **Minor**; move the rupee one tile.
3. **Rockfall is deadlier than §12 says.** Screen ow:3,1. Expected: §12 ranks Deep Wood, Key Room and Gnarl as the death spots. Saw: after Crossroads (−1) and Deep Wood (−2) I reached Rockfall on 1.5 hearts every pass; the unplanned death was there (hp 3 → 0 in 220 frames), with the Octo at (5,1) firing down the only row-1/row-3 lanes and the Brute at (7,8) chasing in a room full of rocks that block knockback. Infer: the route's attrition budget (6 hp) is spent before Rockfall; Deep Wood is survivable but leaves you weak for the next screen. **Major** for a first-time player, minor for a repeat player (the Heart Container detour fixes it, and the key/door/boss progress survive death so nothing is lost but walking).
4. **Gnarl can be stun-locked.** Screen dg:1,0. Expected: §6.4 estimates 6–10 s for an aggressive player and 2–3 hits per cycle. Saw: standing at x≈170, y = boss.y+20 (below the mouth line, outside the contact box), six hits landed 30–36 frames apart with the boss never leaving Patrol; killed in 2.9 s with zero damage, one fan dodged. Infer: because Hurt pauses `spitTimer` (§6.3) and the boss has no knockback, holding Z in reach after the first cooldown suppresses every later spit. **Minor** (the design accepts a fast kill), but if the boss is meant to threaten, let `spitTimer` run during Hurt or push the player back on hit.
5. **Cave and dungeon floors are the same blue as the lake water.** Screens cave:sword, cave:heart, dg:*. Expected: §7 says floor uses fill `b` (cave/dungeon) and water is `water` on `B`. Saw: the floor is a flat bright blue (`cave-sword-hold.png`, `dungeon-entrance.png`); I did not visit Still Lake or Reed Lake so I could not compare the water tile side by side. Infer: a player who has seen the lake first may hesitate to step onto dungeon floor. **Cosmetic**; a darker fill or a floor pattern would settle it.
6. **Brute re-hits on the first free frame.** Screen ow:2,1. Expected: §4.7 gives 60 i-frames and a 32 px knockback. Saw: three hits exactly 60 frames apart while standing still (frames 934/994/1054); the Brute's 1.0 px/f chase closes 32 px well inside 60 frames. Infer: a stunned or confused player loses a heart per second to one Brute; two Brutes in Deep Wood is the intended first wall and it works as such. **Minor**, working as designed.
7. **Trees sit in black squares.** Screen ow:*. Expected: §7 tree tile; sprites.md. Saw: each tree tile has a black background square on the sand-coloured ground (`playing-start.png`). # Tiny Legend — lead plan

Session: `Action Rpg Design` (ref `d1ca90b2-1d1c-4497-b6db-24cb0bbbb74a`, project `rpg-test`).
Goal (verbatim from the operator): _"plan, build and test a small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda. Pull in whatever roles are necessary."_

## 1. Where the game lives and why

The session worktree is a checkout of the TankLoop monorepo (septic-pumping SaaS). The game is a foreign body there, so it is fully self-contained:

- Everything under `games/zelda-like/`. **No file outside this directory is touched by any seat.**

## 2. Scope — the MVP

"Small" is a feature, not a shortcoming. Anything not listed is out of scope until the MVP is verified end to end.

| Area | MVP |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | Browser, HTML5 Canvas 2D, TypeScript strict. No game engine. |
| Presentation | 256×240 virtual NES resolution, integer-scaled to the window, `image-rendering: pixelated`. 16×16 tiles. Play area 16×11 tiles (256×176) under a 64px HUD (hearts, rupees, keys). |
| Art | Programmatic pixel art: sprites and tiles defined as string arrays with a small palette. No binary asset pipeline. |
| Controls | Arrows/WASD move (4-direction, free movement with tile collision). `Z`/`J` sword. `Enter` start/pause. |
| Player | 3 hearts to start, max 5 via heart containers. Sword = short-lived hitbox in facing direction. Taking damage = knockback + ~1s invincibility. |
| Enemies | 3 types + 1 boss: a wanderer that stops and shoots (Octorok-like), an erratic flier (Keese-like), a chaser with 2 HP (Moblin-like). Boss: 6 HP, spits projectiles, in the dungeon. Enemies may drop a heart or rupee. |
| World | Overworld 4×3 = 12 screens with NES edge-scroll transitions. One dungeon of 6 rooms: entrance, two combat rooms, key room, locked door → boss room → treasure room. Maps are ASCII strings, one char per tile. A cave on the first screen holds the sword. |
| Items | Sword, Small Key, Heart (pickup), Heart Container, Rupee, the Artifact (win item). |
| Game states | Title → Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver → Title; Playing → Win → Title. |
| Win / lose | Win: pick up the Artifact in the treasure room. Lose: hearts reach 0 → Game Over; restart from the overworld start screen with 3 hearts, progress (items, keys, cleared boss) kept. |
| Audio | Stretch only: WebAudio bleeps for sword, hit, pickup, door. |
| Persistence | None. |

## 3. Non-negotiable technical shape (architect refines, does not overturn)

1. **Headless simulation core.** All game rules live in pure TypeScript with no DOM or canvas dependency and a fixed 60 Hz step: `step(state, input) → state'` (or an equivalent mutable world with a `tick(input)`). Rendering and input are thin adapters. This is what makes the game testable.
2. **Deterministic.** Any randomness goes through a seedable RNG in the state. Same seed + same input sequence = same outcome.
3. **Data-driven content.** Rooms, enemy placements and item placements are data (ASCII maps + tables), not code branches.
4. **File shape.** Every `.ts` under 300 lines, modules split by concern (player, enemies, combat, rooms, items, hud, render, input, loop).

| Scripted playthrough: seeded RNG + recorded input sequence drives the headless core from Title to Win | Vitest | builder | one test proves the game is completable |
| Type + lint | `tsc --noEmit`, root `oxlint games/zelda-like` | builder | clean |
| Browser smoke: page loads, canvas has pixels, a key press moves the player (via a `window.__game` debug handle) | Playwright | project-setup scaffolds, builder keeps green | `pnpm test:e2e` green |
| Human-style run: launch dev server, play to the dungeon, screenshot each state | runner | screenshots + notes in report |
| Exploratory: try to break it (wall clipping, transition spam, pause abuse, death during transition) | poker | findings list, severity-ranked |
| Acceptance: every row of §2 demonstrably true, every gate above green, evidence cited | verifier | verdict on the wire |

# Tiny Legend

A small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda, running in the browser on a 256×240 canvas with no runtime dependencies.

## Run

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:5173
```

`pnpm build` type-checks and writes a production bundle to `dist/`; `pnpm preview` serves it on port 4173.

## Test

```sh
pnpm typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
pnpm test       # Vitest unit tests (tests/**/*.test.ts)
pnpm test:e2e   # Playwright browser smoke (e2e/**), builds and serves the bundle itself
```

Playwright uses the Chromium build already cached on this host; do not run `playwright install`.

- [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) — scope, phases, test strategy, decisions (lead).

## Layout

- `src/main.ts` — entry point; boots the canvas and (for now) draws a placeholder room.
- `src/render/` — canvas setup and integer scaling.
- `src/core/` — headless simulation (owned by the architect/builder).
- `tests/` — Vitest unit tests. `e2e/` — Playwright specs.

## The goal you serve

Operator's request, verbatim: _"plan, build and test a small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda."_ The game is built, 91 unit tests and 2 browser tests are green, and a recorded playthrough reaches Win. Those prove the happy path. Your job is the unhappy paths: find the inputs and states that make the game misbehave, and hand back deterministic repros.

## Read first

1. `git merge nes-rpg-plan-lead` in your worktree (head `dd58a4e81e63c58bf7d1ba4cd24f02e82ab46607`). `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`; confirm `pnpm test` is 91/91 before you start.

**Collision & movement**

## The goal you serve

Operator's request, verbatim: _"plan, build and test a small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda."_ You own the **content design**: what the world is, what's in it, and how it behaves — written precisely enough that a builder who has never talked to you can implement it from the document alone.

## Read first

1. Your worktree is a checkout of the `rpg-test` repository (the game is the whole repo). Run `git merge nes-rpg-plan-lead` in your worktree to receive the lead's plan (branch head `64c9e9c6396f68491b41edb7c007018496a257a5`, based on `main` @ `340a064`), then read `docs/PLAN.md` — §2 (scope) and §3 (technical shape) bind you.
2. Two other seats work in parallel: an architect (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `src/core/types.ts`) and project-setup (package scaffold). You do not depend on them and they do not depend on you. Your files: `docs/DESIGN.md` (split into `docs/design/*.md` only if a single file passes ~600 lines). **Nothing else.**

## Deliverable

`docs/DESIGN.md`. Contents, in this order:

1. **One-paragraph pitch** and the fantasy (lone hero, retrieve the Artifact from the dungeon).
2. **Controls** — exact key mapping (arrows + WASD move; `Z`/`J` sword; `Enter` start/pause), what each does in each game state.
3. **Game states & flow** — Title → Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver → Title; Playing → Win → Title. What each screen shows, what input advances it, timings (e.g. game-over hold 2 s before accepting input).
4. **Player** — speed in px/frame at 60 Hz, hitbox in px (NES Link is a 16×16 sprite with a ~12×12 body box — pick and state), 4 facings, sword hitbox size/offset per facing and active frames, damage taken (1 heart or ½ heart per source), knockback distance/frames, invincibility frames, death.
5. **Hearts & items** — start 3 hearts, cap 5. Table of every item: Sword, Small Key, Heart (pickup, heals 1), Heart Container (+1 max, fills), Rupee (counter only, cap 255), Artifact (win). For each: where it appears, pickup rule, HUD effect.
6. **Enemies** — exactly three overworld/dungeon types + one boss, each with: name, HP, damage dealt, speed, hitbox, behaviour as a state machine (states, transitions, timers in frames), projectile stats if any, drop table (percent heart / rupee / nothing), which rooms they appear in. Suggested archetypes: wanderer-that-stops-and-shoots (Octorok-like), erratic flier (Keese-like), 2-HP chaser (Moblin-like), boss with 6 HP that spits projectiles in a pattern. Boss must be beatable with the basic sword by a careful player in under ~60 s.
7. **Tile legend** — one ASCII character per tile type, with: passable?, blocks projectiles?, visual (a name; the palette is yours), special behaviour (door, locked door, stairs/cave entrance, water, etc.). Keep it under ~12 tile types.
8. **World maps** — every screen as a 16-wide × 11-high ASCII block using the legend. Overworld: 4 columns × 3 rows = 12 screens, coordinates `(col,row)` with the start position stated; screens connect by edges (walking off the edge scrolls to the neighbour) so edge tiles must line up. Include: start screen with a cave entrance holding the Sword; a hidden Heart Container; the dungeon entrance. Dungeon: 6 rooms — entrance, two combat rooms, key room, locked door leading to boss room, treasure room with the Artifact — same 16×11 format, with door positions and which are locked. Provide a small overview grid for each map showing how rooms connect.
9. **Spawns** — per screen: enemies (type, tile position) and items (type, tile position). Spawn rule (respawn on re-entry? NES respawns; state whether the boss stays dead — it must).
10. **HUD** — 64px-tall strip: heart row, rupee counter, key counter, mini-map optional. Positions in px.
11. **Palette** — ≤ 16 named colours as hex, NES-flavoured. Sprites will be drawn programmatically from text, so also give an **8×8 or 16×16 ASCII sprite** for: player (one facing is enough; others may mirror), each enemy, sword, heart, rupee, key, artifact. Use one character per palette index, `.` for transparent.
12. **Difficulty & pacing** — expected time to win (~5–8 min), where the player is likely to die, what makes the boss fair.
13. **Out of scope** — list what you deliberately left out and why (keeps the builder from guessing).

## Constraints

- Every quantity is a number (frames, px, HP). "Fast" and "a bit" are defects.
- Everything must be representable as data: ASCII maps, tables. No behaviour that needs bespoke scripting beyond the enemy state machines you describe.
- Stay inside PLAN.md §2. If you believe a scope item is wrong for the game, say so in a "Proposed scope changes" appendix — do not silently design around it.
- Write only `docs/DESIGN.md` (or `docs/design/*.md`). Do not create code files. Do not edit `docs/PLAN.md`.

## How to work

- Commit on your own branch with a conventional message: `docs(rpg): game design document`. Do not push to `origin`. Report branch name and commit SHA; the lead integrates.

21	## 2. Scope — the MVP
22	
23	"Small" is a feature, not a shortcoming. Anything not listed is out of scope until the MVP is verified end to end.
24	
25	| Area | MVP |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Platform | Browser, HTML5 Canvas 2D, TypeScript strict. No game engine. |
28	| Presentation | 256×240 virtual NES resolution, integer-scaled to the window, `image-rendering: pixelated`. 16×16 tiles. Play area 16×11 tiles (256×176) under a 64px HUD (hearts, rupees, keys). |
29	| Art | Programmatic pixel art: sprites and tiles defined as string arrays with a small palette. No binary asset pipeline. |
30	| Controls | Arrows/WASD move (4-direction, free movement with tile collision). `Z`/`J` sword. `Enter` start/pause. |
31	| Player | 3 hearts to start, max 5 via heart containers. Sword = short-lived hitbox in facing direction. Taking damage = knockback + ~1s invincibility. |
32	| Enemies | 3 types + 1 boss: a wanderer that stops and shoots (Octorok-like), an erratic flier (Keese-like), a chaser with 2 HP (Moblin-like). Boss: 6 HP, spits projectiles, in the dungeon. Enemies may drop a heart or rupee. |
33	| World | Overworld 4×3 = 12 screens with NES edge-scroll transitions. One dungeon of 6 rooms: entrance, two combat rooms, key room, locked door → boss room → treasure room. Maps are ASCII strings, one char per tile. A cave on the first screen holds the sword. |
34	| Items | Sword, Small Key, Heart (pickup), Heart Container, Rupee, the Artifact (win item). |
35	| Game states | Title → Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver → Title; Playing → Win → Title. |
36	| Win / lose | Win: pick up the Artifact in the treasure room. Lose: hearts reach 0 → Game Over; restart from the overworld start screen with 3 hearts, progress (items, keys, cleared boss) kept. |
37	| Audio | Stretch only: WebAudio bleeps for sword, hit, pickup, door. |
38	| Persistence | None. |

40	## 3. Non-negotiable technical shape (architect refines, does not overturn)
41	
42	1. **Headless simulation core.** All game rules live in pure TypeScript with no DOM or canvas dependency and a fixed 60 Hz step: `step(state, input)` (mutable world) or `step(state, input) → state'`. Rendering and input are thin adapters. This is what makes the game testable.
43	2. **Deterministic.** Any randomness goes through a seedable RNG in the state. Same seed + same input sequence = same outcome. No `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance` in `src/core/**`.
44	3. **Data-driven content.** Rooms, enemy placements and item placements are data (ASCII maps + tables), not code branches.
45	4. **File shape.** Every `.ts` under 300 lines; modules split by concern (player, enemies, combat, rooms, items, hud, render, input, loop).

8. One swing hitting the same enemy twice; one swing hitting two enemies; sword vs. enemy in Hurt/Dying; sword vs. boss during Windup/Spit.

16. Pause on the frame a transition starts / ends; pause during hold; Enter held continuously across Title → Playing → Paused (must not ripple).
17. Opposite keys held; all four held; attack held for 1000 frames (exactly one swing per press).

1	# Tiny Legend — game design document
2	
3	Owner: the `designer` seat. Binds the builder; refines, never overturns, [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §2 (scope) and §3 (technical shape). Companion files (split out because the maps and sprites alone exceed 600 lines):
4	
5	- [`design/maps.md`](design/maps.md) — §8 world maps (all 20 screens as 16×11 ASCII) and §9 spawns, with a self-check script.
6	- [`design/sprites.md`](design/sprites.md) — §11 palette and every sprite as ASCII, with a self-check script.
7	
8	Conventions used everywhere: the game runs at a fixed 60 Hz; every duration is in **frames** (60 = 1 s). Distances are in **px** at the virtual 256×240 resolution. A tile is 16×16 px. The play area is 16×11 tiles = 256×176 px, drawn at canvas y = 64..239 under the 64-px HUD; **all entity positions in this document are play-area coordinates** (add 64 to y when drawing). Hit points of the player are counted in **half-hearts** (`hp`), enemies in **sword hits**. All randomness uses the seeded RNG in the state (`rng.int(lo, hi)` = integer in `[lo, hi]` inclusive; `rng.pct()` = integer in `[0, 99]`).
9	
10	## 1. Pitch
11	
12	A lone hero wakes in a meadow with nothing. In a cave on that same meadow lies a sword. North-east, past a forest full of Brutes and a rockfall, a dungeon door is set into the mountain; inside, six rooms, a key, a locked door, and Gnarl the Cave Wyrm, who guards the Sunstone — the Artifact. Pick it up and the land is saved. That is the whole game: get the sword, cross the overworld, find the key, unlock the door, beat the boss, take the Artifact. A hidden second cave holds a Heart Container for those who explore. Five to eight minutes for a first clear, one screen at a time, NES Zelda rules: enemies respawn when you re-enter a screen, hearts are precious, and the sword is the only weapon.
13	
14	## 2. Controls
15	
16	Keyboard only. Input is sampled once per frame into `{ up, down, left, right, sword, start }` (held booleans) plus `swordPressed`, `startPressed` (true only on the frame the key went down — edge-triggered). Key repeat from the OS is ignored.
17	
18	| Action | Keys | Playing | Paused | Title / GameOver / Win |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| Move up | `ArrowUp`, `W` | move / face up | — | — |
21	| Move down | `ArrowDown`, `S` | move / face down | — | — |
22	| Move left | `ArrowLeft`, `A` | move / face left | — | — |
23	| Move right | `ArrowRight`, `D` | move / face right | — | — |
24	| Sword | `Z`, `J` (pressed) | swing (needs `hasSword`) | — | — |
25	| Start | `Enter` (pressed) | pause | resume | advance (see §3) |
26	
27	- Opposite keys held together cancel (no movement on that axis). When one horizontal and one vertical key are held, **vertical wins**; there is no diagonal movement.
28	- The browser default for arrow keys, space and Enter is prevented so the page never scrolls.
29	- No mouse or touch input. No gamepad. (Out of scope, §13.)
30	
31	## 3. Game states and flow
32	
33	```
34	        Enter                 Enter                  hp = 0
35	Title ───────► Playing ◄──────────► Paused     Playing ─────► GameOver ──Enter (after 120 f)──► Title
36	   ▲                                                                                                │
37	   └──────────────── Enter (after 120 f) ─── Win ◄──── Artifact hold ends ──── Playing ◄────────────┘
38	```
39	
40	Every state renders the full 256×240 canvas. All text is white unless stated; `PRESS ENTER` prompts blink (visible 30 frames, hidden 30 frames). Text is drawn with the renderer's own 8-px font (§10.3).
41	
42	| State | Shows | Input accepted | Transition |
43	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
44	| **Title** | Black. `TINY LEGEND` centred at y=72. `player-down` sprite at (120,104). `PRESS ENTER` centred at y=168. If `progress` exists (a Game Over happened this session), a second line `CONTINUE` at y=184 instead of nothing. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames of the state | → Playing. With no `progress`: a fresh `World` (seed from `Date.now()` in the adapter, passed into the core). With `progress`: new `World` with the progress fields restored (§3.1), player at the start position with 6 hp. |
45	| **Playing** | HUD (§10) + current screen + entities. | all | Enter → Paused. `hp` reaches 0 → death sequence (§4.8) → GameOver. Artifact hold ends → Win. |
46	| **Paused** | The frozen Playing frame, plus `PAUSED` centred at y=160 (play-area y=96). Nothing updates. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames | → Playing (nothing in the world changed). |
47	| **GameOver** | Black. `GAME OVER` in `R` centred at y=104. After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=168. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` set (§3.1). |
48	| **Win** | Black. `YOU FOUND THE SUNSTONE` centred at y=88; `THE LAND IS SAVED` at y=104; `artifact` sprite at (120,128). After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=176. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` cleared (the next start is a fresh game). |
49	
50	Sub-states inside Playing (not separate top-level states; Enter is ignored while they run):
51	
52	| Sub-state | Duration | What happens |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| **Scroll** (screen edge) | 32 frames | The old and new screens are drawn side by side and slide 8 px per frame (256/32 horizontally; 176/32 = 5.5 px per frame vertically). No entity updates. The player sprite is drawn at its arrival position on the new screen, moving with it. Enemies of the old screen are discarded on frame 0; the new screen's enemies spawn on frame 32. |
55	| **Warp** (`C`/`D`/`X`) | 20 frames | Play area black; HUD still drawn. On frame 20 the destination screen is loaded and its enemies spawn. |
56	| **Hold** (big item pickup) | 60 frames | §5.3. Nothing moves except the timer. |
57	| **Dying** | 60 frames | §4.8. |
58	
59	### 3.1 Progress kept across Game Over
60	
61	`progress = { hasSword, maxHp, rupees, keys, collectedItems, unlockedDoors, bossDefeated, visitedScreens }`. Restored on continue. Not kept: current hp (reset to 6), current screen and position (reset to start), live enemies, drops, the boss's current hp (it is either dead or full).
62	
63	## 4. Player
64	
65	### 4.1 Numbers
66	
67	| Property | Value |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| Sprite | 16×16, `player-<facing>` |
70	| Hitbox | 12×12 at offset (2,2) from the sprite's top-left |
71	| Position | `x, y` floats (px, play area); drawn at `Math.floor` |
72	| Speed | 1.5 px/frame while a direction is held and not blocked |
73	| Facings | up, down, left, right; changes to the held direction on any frame the player moves or tries to move (blocked movement still turns) |
74	| Start hp / max hp | 6 / 6 (3 hearts); max hp cap 10 (5 hearts) |
75	| Start position | screen `ow:1,2`, sprite at (112,112), facing up (maps.md §8.1) |
76	
77	### 4.2 Movement and tile collision
78	
79	Each frame, if not in Swing, Knockback, Hold or Dying: compute the intended delta (±1.5 on one axis). Move on that axis, then resolve against solid tiles: for every tile overlapped by the hitbox after the move, if the tile is solid (§7), push the hitbox back flush against that tile's edge and stop. Tiles outside the 16×11 grid are treated as **passable for the player** so that walking off the edge triggers a Scroll (§4.3). Conditional tiles: `L` is solid unless `keys > 0`, in which case touching it consumes a key (§5.2); `S` is solid while any enemy on the screen is alive; `C`, `D`, `X` are passable and trigger a Warp when the hitbox **centre** lies inside them.
80	
81	Optional polish (slice d, not required): NES-style corner nudge — when blocked while moving along an axis, if the hitbox overlaps the blocking tile by ≤ 4 px on the perpendicular axis, slide 1 px per frame on that axis away from the tile instead of stopping.
82

21	## 2. Scope — the MVP
22	
23	"Small" is a feature, not a shortcoming. Anything not listed is out of scope until the MVP is verified end to end.
24	
25	| Area | MVP |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Platform | Browser, HTML5 Canvas 2D, TypeScript strict. No game engine. |
28	| Presentation | 256×240 virtual NES resolution, integer-scaled to the window, `image-rendering: pixelated`. 16×16 tiles. Play area 16×11 tiles (256×176) under a 64px HUD (hearts, rupees, keys). |
29	| Art | Programmatic pixel art: sprites and tiles defined as string arrays with a small palette. No binary asset pipeline. |
30	| Controls | Arrows/WASD move (4-direction, free movement with tile collision). `Z`/`J` sword. `Enter` start/pause. |
31	| Player | 3 hearts to start, max 5 via heart containers. Sword = short-lived hitbox in facing direction. Taking damage = knockback + ~1s invincibility. |
32	| Enemies | 3 types + 1 boss: a wanderer that stops and shoots (Octorok-like), an erratic flier (Keese-like), a chaser with 2 HP (Moblin-like). Boss: 6 HP, spits projectiles, in the dungeon. Enemies may drop a heart or rupee. |
33	| World | Overworld 4×3 = 12 screens with NES edge-scroll transitions. One dungeon of 6 rooms: entrance, two combat rooms, key room, locked door → boss room → treasure room. Maps are ASCII strings, one char per tile. A cave on the first screen holds the sword. |
34	| Items | Sword, Small Key, Heart (pickup), Heart Container, Rupee, the Artifact (win item). |
35	| Game states | Title → Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver → Title; Playing → Win → Title. |
36	| Win / lose | Win: pick up the Artifact in the treasure room. Lose: hearts reach 0 → Game Over; restart from the overworld start screen with 3 hearts, progress (items, keys, cleared boss) kept. |
37	| Audio | Stretch only: WebAudio bleeps for sword, hit, pickup, door. |
38	| Persistence | None. |

40	## 3. Non-negotiable technical shape (architect refines, does not overturn)
41	
42	1. **Headless simulation core.** All game rules live in pure TypeScript with no DOM or canvas dependency and a fixed 60 Hz step: `step(state, input)` (mutable world) or `step(state, input) → state'`. Rendering and input are thin adapters. This is what makes the game testable.
43	2. **Deterministic.** Any randomness goes through a seedable RNG in the state. Same seed + same input sequence = same outcome. No `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance` in `src/core/**`.
44	3. **Data-driven content.** Rooms, enemy placements and item placements are data (ASCII maps + tables), not code branches.
45	4. **File shape.** Every `.ts` under 300 lines; modules split by concern (player, enemies, combat, rooms, items, hud, render, input, loop).
46

21	## 2. Scope — the MVP
22	
23	"Small" is a feature, not a shortcoming. Anything not listed is out of scope until the MVP is verified end to end.
24	
25	| Area | MVP |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Platform | Browser, HTML5 Canvas 2D, TypeScript strict. No game engine. |
28	| Presentation | 256×240 virtual NES resolution, integer-scaled to the window, `image-rendering: pixelated`. 16×16 tiles. Play area 16×11 tiles (256×176) under a 64px HUD (hearts, rupees, keys). |
29	| Art | Programmatic pixel art: sprites and tiles defined as string arrays with a small palette. No binary asset pipeline. |
30	| Controls | Arrows/WASD move (4-direction, free movement with tile collision). `Z`/`J` sword. `Enter` start/pause. |
31	| Player | 3 hearts to start, max 5 via heart containers. Sword = short-lived hitbox in facing direction. Taking damage = knockback + ~1s invincibility. |
32	| Enemies | 3 types + 1 boss: a wanderer that stops and shoots (Octorok-like), an erratic flier (Keese-like), a chaser with 2 HP (Moblin-like). Boss: 6 HP, spits projectiles, in the dungeon. Enemies may drop a heart or rupee. |
33	| World | Overworld 4×3 = 12 screens with NES edge-scroll transitions. One dungeon of 6 rooms: entrance, two combat rooms, key room, locked door → boss room → treasure room. Maps are ASCII strings, one char per tile. A cave on the first screen holds the sword. |
34	| Items | Sword, Small Key, Heart (pickup), Heart Container, Rupee, the Artifact (win item). |
35	| Game states | Title → Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver → Title; Playing → Win → Title. |
36	| Win / lose | Win: pick up the Artifact in the treasure room. Lose: hearts reach 0 → Game Over; restart from the overworld start screen with 3 hearts, progress (items, keys, cleared boss) kept. |
37	| Audio | Stretch only: WebAudio bleeps for sword, hit, pickup, door. |
38	| Persistence | None. |

40	## 3. Non-negotiable technical shape (architect refines, does not overturn)
41	
42	1. **Headless simulation core.** All game rules live in pure TypeScript with no DOM or canvas dependency and a fixed 60 Hz step: `step(state, input)` (mutable world) or `step(state, input) → state'`. Rendering and input are thin adapters. This is what makes the game testable.
43	2. **Deterministic.** Any randomness goes through a seedable RNG in the state. Same seed + same input sequence = same outcome. No `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance` in `src/core/**`.
44	3. **Data-driven content.** Rooms, enemy placements and item placements are data (ASCII maps + tables), not code branches.
45	4. **File shape.** Every `.ts` under 300 lines; modules split by concern (player, enemies, combat, rooms, items, hud, render, input, loop).

3. Sub-pixel drift: hold a direction for 10 000 frames against a wall; does `x`/`y` stay exact and inside the field?
4. Walking off an edge that has no neighbour (world border) — is it always solid?

11. Projectile edge cases: Octo "one live Rock" rule when the Rock is off-screen after a transition; fireballs surviving a transition; projectile spawned inside a wall.

12. Locked door with 0 keys, with 2 keys (only one consumed), approaching from the far side (mirrored tile) — both `L` tiles replaced in both rooms.
13. Shutter `S`: passable only when no live enemy; what about enemies in Dying phase? Retreat and re-enter the boss room after killing the boss: `S` open, boss absent, no second Heart drop.
14. Rupees at 255, maxHp at 10 (cap), hearts pickup at full hp, key counter with the HUD.
15. Drop TTL expiry mid-pickup; drop spawned on a solid tile or off-field.

**Modes & input**
16. Pause on the frame a transition starts / ends; pause during hold; Enter held continuously across Title → Playing → Paused (must not ripple).
17. Opposite keys held; all four held; attack held for 1000 frames (exactly one swing per press).
